title: Python slot_claim decode_cose accepts ordinal-less COSE claims; corpus vector ordinal_absent mandates rejection
description: Discovered by worker-1 while landing the Rust vector-mirror test (l1qw.16.2.4): test/vectors/gcp_slot_claim_cose_sign1.json case 'ordinal_absent' (payload keys 1..6, mode 0, no key 7) is expected_reject_reason=ordinal_missing with description 'MUST reject as malformed - the receiver cannot register the gateway'. Rust RawSlotClaim::from_cose now rejects it (key 7 required, landed in l1qw.16.2.4). Python parity gap: python/src/lichen/gateway/slot_claim.py decode_cose (lines 254-256) treats ordinal as optional (fields.get(_PAYLOAD_ORDINAL) -> None accepted), and encode_claim_canonical (lines 301-311) omits key 7 when claim.ordinal is None - so a Python-encoded ordinal-less claim would be accepted by Python but rejected by Rust and by the shared corpus. Fix: decode_cose must raise ClaimError when _PAYLOAD_ORDINAL is absent (keys 1-7 all required), and encode/sign paths must require a non-None ordinal (SlotClaim constructor or sign_slot_claim fail-closed). Mirror the vector corpus in a python test (python/tests consuming gcp_slot_claim_cose_sign1.json — no consumer exists yet). Check python/tests/test_vectors.py for the corpus-runner pattern. NOTE for l1qw.16.2.2: Rust SlotClaim::encode_cose has the mirror-image gap — it omits key 7 when with_federation was not called, producing envelopes that spec receivers (and from_cose) now reject; make encode_cose require the ordinal.
